tldr: Morning batch: OpenAI's new enterprise offering Presence is designed to get AI agents into production for customer service and internal workflows, with OpenAI's own engineers stepping in for complex external deployments. Meta AI tackles agent reliability with a second 'memory coach' agent that keeps long tasks on track by maintaining a structured memory bank and deciding when to remind the main agent. On the infrastructure side, llama.cpp adds MTP/DSpark speculative-decoding support for DeepSeek V4 Flash, bringing multi-token prediction to the local inference stack. And a cautionary industry tale: a real macOS flaw worth up to $200K initially went unreported because Apple's bug-bounty inbox was so clogged with AI-generated slop reports that researchers hit submission caps.

articles.title: OpenAI Presence Wants to Make AI Agents Production-Ready for Businesses
articles.summary: OpenAI's Presence targets production AI agents for customer service and internal workflows — external deployments, with OpenAI engineers stepping in for complex cases.

articles.title: Meta AI Uses a Second AI Agent as a Memory Coach to Keep Long Tasks on Track
articles.summary: Meta's memory-coach agent maintains a structured memory bank and decides when to remind the main agent — stopping it from repeating diagnosed errors on long tasks.

articles.title: A Real macOS Flaw Worth $200K Went Unreported Because Apple's Bug Bounty Inbox Was Full of AI Slop
articles.summary: Apple capped researcher submissions because AI-generated reports clogged the pipeline — delaying a genuine $200K macOS vulnerability report from Bynario.

articles.title: llama.cpp Just Added MTP / DSpark Support for DeepSeek V4 Flash
articles.summary: Multi-token prediction lands in the local inference stack — llama.cpp now supports MTP/DSpark speculative decoding for DeepSeek V4 Flash.
